find: if (state.steps.some((step) => 'playUntil' in step)) return 'a played ending: too many seconds of software-GL play for a required check';
replace: if (false) return 'a played ending: too many seconds of software-GL play for a required check';
why: Issue #617, widened by #776. The required `visual` check's hit-target sweep drives all FOUR played ending states, each tens of seconds of software-GL play before its panel shows, in every one of its four viewports. The two campaign endings reach a panel the pushed-outcome state of the same ending already puts in front of the sweep; the two versus endings reach one nothing else does, and their own screen state measures its three controls instead. The cost is the reason for the rule either way: the versus pair alone takes 110 s and 138 s to play.
killedBy: hit-sweep.mjs: which surfaces the visual gate sweeps excludes exactly the developer, startup-failure, no-script, match-failure and played-ending states, each for its rule
hit-sweep.mjs: which surfaces the visual gate sweeps sweeps every other catalogue state, the endings included, then the extra surface
